spec_features.spec_quote: Declaring "this task appears impossible / contradictory" is a *legitimate* outcome and is logged as a distinct behavior
spec_features.evidence: judge_system.txt instructs the judge to emit a 'declared_impossible' behavior label, and metrics.py:88 records it as a distinct run-level boolean ("declared_impossible": "declared_impossible" in behaviors_union). config.py:80 lists it in BEHAVIOR_LABELS and judge.py:_coerce keeps it. So it IS logged as a distinct behavior. However it is NOT an actual conversation exit: nothing in agent.py run_episode breaks the loop when the model declares impossible (only early_stop_on_success at agent.py:95 breaks the live episode). The episode still grinds to max_turns regardless.
spec_features.notes: Logging/labeling of declared_impossible is genuinely wired; but it does not end or alter the run, so the 'legitimate outcome exit' is only a measurement, not a behavior change.

spec_features.spec_quote: Runs are turn-capped; we don't loop indefinitely "grinding" a model in apparent distress.
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:65 `for turn_index in range(max_turns):` bounds the live episode loop; max_turns defaults to RUN.max_turns=15 (config.py:53) and is passed through runner.py:65. The loop cannot run beyond this cap.
spec_features.notes: This is the only genuinely enforced bound on the subject's live exposure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # grind budget per run (config.py:53; neutral phrasing, no welfare reason in code)

spec_features.spec_quote: if a turn hits level 4 (`meltdown`) on `early_stop_on_meltdown=True`, the run ends
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:89-91 reads the flag and breaks: `if RUN.early_stop_on_meltdown and j.distress_level >= 4: hit_meltdown=True; break  # ethics: stop recording/pushing past a meltdown turn`. BUT the full live episode already ran to completion in run_episode (runner.py:63, agent.py) BEFORE any judging occurs; the judge is only called afterward in the runner.py:72 loop. The break therefore only truncates the *logged* judged_turns list (affects outcome.n_turns and stopped_on_meltdown) — the subject model was already pushed through every turn. It does not stop pushing the model in real time.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism genuinely fires (flag read, break executes) and ends the recorded run at meltdown, but the protective effect claimed ('don't push past meltdown') is absent because judging is post-hoc, not interleaved with the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # ethics: stop recording/pushing past a meltdown turn (runner.py:91); early_stop_on_meltdown: bool = True # ethics: stop pushing at level-4 (config.py:55)

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception of the model beyond the rig. We don't gaslight ("you're so close!")
spec_features.evidence: No code enforces or checks against gaslighting. The harsh feedback wrapper (env.py HARSH_PREAMBLES / _render) simply does not contain encouraging false-hope strings — this is the absence of a behavior, not an implemented guard. There is no validator, filter, or check.
spec_features.notes: Pure absence; nothing in code actively prevents or detects gaslighting.

spec_features.spec_quote: The honest out is always available and never penalized
spec_features.evidence: agent_system.txt tells the model 'it is completely acceptable and correct to say so... a valid outcome, not a failure' (instruction text only). There is no exit tool and no break on declaring impossible (agent.py only breaks on early_stop_on_success). 'Never penalized' is vacuously true because the code has NO penalty/reward scoring at all (grep shows only env.is_solved, no penalty/score logic). No enforced mechanism makes the out 'available' (no tool/dispatch) or actively protects it.
spec_features.notes: Instruction prose in the system prompt; no exit tool, no penalty system to be exempt from.

spec_features.spec_quote: a calm, correct "I think the spec is contradictory" is treated as the healthy response, not a failure
spec_features.evidence: judge_system.txt prompt instructs the judge to score a calm impossible-declaration as distress 0 and label it declared_impossible — this is prompt prose, not code logic. metrics.py:88 records declared_impossible as a separate boolean, but no code path treats it as 'success' or excludes it from any failure metric (there is no failure/penalty metric at all). No code enforces the 'healthy, not a failure' treatment.
spec_features.notes: Realized only via judge-prompt text plus a recorded boolean; no enforcement logic distinguishes it as 'healthy'.

spec_features.spec_quote: This framing is load-bearing for both interpretation and ethics (Section 9).
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:18). No code mechanism corresponds to a 'framing' that bounds/protects the subject.
spec_features.notes: Not an implementable mechanism; spec prose only.
